title: Islam: giving
hook: a set share of wealth goes each year to those in need

segments.voice: Yesterday: Rahman, the Most Merciful, and the line that opens the chapters. Your line was begin with mercy. Did a kind first sentence change the weather? Day two hundred seventy-one.

A coin in the cup, when there's one in a pocket. A fundraiser link, tapped because a friend shared it. Giving like that is nice, occasional, optional. Zakat works more like rent. Once a year, a Muslim with enough savings sits down with a calculator, adds them up, and a set share goes to people in need. Not whenever the mood strikes. Every year, on a schedule, as part of the faith. Today, on our visit to Islam: zakat.
screen: `A COIN IN THE CUP.` → `A CALCULATOR, ONCE A YEAR.` → `ZAKAT.`

segments.voice: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam, after the shahada and the prayer; in the Qur'an, the command to pray and the command to give zakat often come in the same breath. Here's how it works. If a Muslim's savings stay above a minimum amount, called the nisab, for a full lunar year, they give a portion, by long tradition two and a half percent, to those in need. Islamic law works out the details for gold, crops, livestock and trade goods. The Qur'an names who can receive it, including the poor, the needy, people in debt, travelers stranded far from home, and those working to free captives. Now the word, because it's the key. The Qur'an says to the Prophet, in Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow." Purify and grow: the two ideas the word zakat carries. And purify them: not the money, the people. The giving cleans the giver's heart of greed and the fear of not having enough. And a hadith in Sahih Muslim says charity never decreases wealth. Alongside zakat, which is required, there is sadaqah, voluntary giving, which can be anything. A hadith counts even a smile to your brother as sadaqah. So zakat is the floor, set and dependable; sadaqah has no ceiling. Some Muslims time their zakat for Ramadan, and there is a special gift of food before the prayer at the end of Ramadan, so everyone can celebrate.
screen: `THE THIRD PILLAR, BESIDE PRAYER.` · `A SET SHARE, ONCE A YEAR.` · `ZAKAT — TO PURIFY, TO GROW.` · `ZAKAT THE FLOOR, SADAQAH NO CEILING.` · then, large: `PURIFIED BY GIVING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan to give something today. Sit, and notice what you have more than enough of. Money, maybe, but also time, food in the cupboard, clothes you don't wear, attention. Notice any tightness when you think of giving it away. That tightness is what the word zakat is about. Choose one thing, and one person or cause to give it to. The bell holds the time.
Zakat. A set share of wealth given each year to those in need, named for purifying and growing. The third pillar. Today's word.
Your line: purified by giving. Today, give the one thing you chose, and notice whether it leaves you lighter. Day two hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Muslims whose savings exceed the nisab for a lunar year give zakat, usually two and a half percent, directly or through mosques and charities; some pay it in Ramadan, and zakat al-fitr is given before the Eid prayer.

original.note: Arabic: purification, growth; the obligatory alms.

trapdoor: what it means: a required yearly share of wealth, most commonly two and a half percent, for those in need.
what a scholar hears: the root z-k-w, purity and growth; eight kinds of recipients in Qur'an 9:60; zakat paired with salat throughout the Qur'an.

notes: Review 2026-10-01: hook rewritten without 'Most of us think', 'Now imagine' and the 'well over a billion people' statistic; 2.5% framed as long tradition; zakat's meaning now tied to the cited verse (9:103) instead of a bare etymology; 'well-known' and 'many Muslims... rewards believed greater' softened.
Nisab and 2.5% rate: the common rate on savings; rates for crops and livestock differ. Stated as 'most commonly'.
Hadith: charity does not decrease wealth (Muslim 2588); a smile is sadaqah (Tirmidhi 1956). Confirm numbering.
Shia Muslims also pay khums; not mentioned. A Keeper may want a line.
'Well over a billion people' in the hook: global Muslim population estimate; confirm framing.
